title: Nudge
author: Richard H. Thaler and Cass R. Sunstein

sections.title: The Tools of the Choice Architect

chapters.title: When Do We Need a Nudge?
Do Nudges Last Forever? Perhaps in Sweden
Borrow More Today: Mortgages and Credit Cards
Insurance: Don't Sweat the Small Stuff
Organ Donations: The Default Solution Illusion

thesis: Choices are never presented neutrally: defaults, ordering, feedback, social cues, and administrative friction predictably shape what fallible people do. Institutions can therefore design environments that improve decisions while keeping meaningful alternatives available and avoiding large changes to economic incentives.
teachingArc: Part I replaces the perfectly calculating Econ with a psychologically realistic Human who relies on shortcuts, struggles with self-control, and follows others. Part II turns those limits into a design discipline through choice architecture, disclosure, and sludge reduction; Parts III and IV apply the tools to saving, borrowing, insurance, organ donation, and climate policy. Part V tests ethical and political objections, arguing for transparent, welfare-oriented nudges that preserve choice and can complement stronger policy tools.

signatureMoves: opens concepts with ordinary decisions or vivid institutional cases
contrasts idealized Econs with predictably fallible Humans
uses playful labels and acronyms to make policy mechanisms memorable
moves from behavioral evidence to a concrete design or policy proposal
anticipates objections and answers them with counterexamples
avoidMoves: does not rely on a purely academic register
does not treat freedom and paternalism as an unavoidable binary
does not present nudges as substitutes for every mandate or incentive

notes: The 2021 Penguin paperback Final Edition is used because the slug did not specify an edition and this is the current cover-to-cover revision.
